messages:
joel: Quick follow-up to the CP proxy ownership RFC — thinking about a 'slim-proxy' split. We keep auth/handshake in CP proxy, but move egress IP preservation & token minting to tenant-side relay. Benefits: smaller CP surface, easier scale. Risks: more complex relay bootstrapping and cert flow.

anya: Can you list the invariants we need to keep for per-tenant auditing?

joel: Minimal invariants: 1) auditable tenant request ID propagated end-to-end; 2) CP can force-fallback to hosted egress; 3) token minting aud & scope checks cannot be bypassed.

sam: How does cert rotation work for relay? We currently push certs from CP — that tight coupling is what we try to avoid.

meera: Proposal: use short-lived bootstrap token + ACME-ish cert issuance from CP CA. Relay exchanges bootstrap for leaf cert via `handshake.v2`. CP logs issuance events. This keeps CP causal for identity but not for runtime egress.

anya: Does that affect latency on first request? what about cold-starts and SLOs?

joel: Cold-start + bootstrap adds ~50-200ms once per relay lifetime. We can mitigate with pre-provisioned certs for high-tier customers or batched issuance.

ops-team: How to handle emergency revoke (compromised relay)? need ability to cut egress fast.

meera: CP will publish revocation list + short TTL certs. Also recommend adding connection health signals to allow quick blackhole.

sam: What about pricing/infra ownership? more relays means more NAT IPs; could be bill shock.

joel: We'll provide a policy: default shared egress for >X customers, reserved egress for enterprise buys. Also add telemetry to estimate allocation costs before commit.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: cp-proxy/handshake spike branch deployed to beta on 2026-01-12. Logs available: https://internal/logs/1749994444

anya: I'm okay to move forward with a small spike. Action items: joel write short RFC add invariants + cert sequence diagrams; meera draft bootstrap token flow; sam quantify SLO delta.

joel: will do. tagging @meera @sam. :thumbsup:
